current.text: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.

predecessors.text: Verify that all sensitive data is identified and classified into protection levels.

Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified, and ensure that a policy is in place on how to deal with sensitive data. ([C8](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

Verify that regulated private data is stored encrypted while at rest, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII), sensitive personal information, or data assessed likely to be subject to EU's GDPR.
Verify that regulated health data is stored encrypted while at rest, such as medical records, medical device details, or de-anonymized research records.

Verify that regulated financial data is stored encrypted while at rest, such as financial accounts, defaults or credit history, tax records, pay history, beneficiaries, or de-anonymized market or research records.

summaries.body:
V14.1.1 is a 5.0 merge of data-classification and regulated-data-at-rest controls. The mapping records MODIFIED, MOVED FROM v4.0.3-1.8.1, MERGED FROM v4.0.3-8.3.4, v4.0.3-6.1.1, v4.0.3-6.1.2, COVERS v4.0.3-6.1.3. V1.8.1 required identifying sensitive data and classifying it into protection levels. V8.3.4 required identifying sensitive data created and processed by the application and having a policy for it. V6.1.1–V6.1.3 required encryption at rest for regulated private, health, and financial data.

The current clause is the identification/classification requirement, expanded to treat easily decoded encodings (Base64, JWT plaintext payloads) as sensitive data, with protection levels taking applicable data-protection and privacy regulations into account. Git first recorded at V6.1.3 (abhay adding CWEs for Authentication, 2019-02-21) is slot noise on one predecessor ID; mapping and predecessor texts are the reliable origin.

The wording change that mattered is the 5.0 fold: architecture-level classification (V1.8.1), a handling policy (V8.3.4), and the three regulated-at-rest encryption checks (V6.1.1–V6.1.3) became one classification control that also names encoded-but-decodable data. tghosth's 2019-02-24 C8 tag on V8.3.4 and janda26's 2020 capitalisation pass on V6.1.1 are not that fold.

Issue #472 (V14.1 subcategory missing) is 4.x Configuration numbering, not this data-protection documentation control. Other V6.1.3-slot events (Grammarly, duplicate-entry removal, L3 tick, CWSS) are editorial or chapter reuse.
